reasons: The formula, its per-variant application, the definitions of delta and variance, the 95% two-sided/80%-power assumptions embodied by 16, and the binomial conversion-rate variance are all stated in the substantive sample-size section.
The dependency on setting an MDE is non-circular and consistent with the source's instruction to set the MDE to the smallest lift worth shipping.

The substantive worked table gives 80,682 visitors per variant for a 2% baseline and 10% relative lift under 95% confidence, 80% power, and a two-sided test; the candidate's approximation to 80,000 is supported.
Its limitation against generalizing this example without recalculation is appropriate.

The recommended constraints are supported: hold external conditions as constant as possible, compare equal/comparable periods, treat a stable shift as a weak signal rather than proof, use pre-post for big structural changes, and later confirm with randomization when traffic allows.

The trigger adds that traffic must be too low for a randomized test. The source says pre-post can help at low volume and recommends later confirmation when traffic allows, but does not make inability to run a randomized test an explicit prerequisite for every use of pre-post testing.
The substantive discussion supports treating 3,000–20,000 monthly orders as a fair volume floor for A/B/n and bandit work.

The stated exception is specifically that bandits can be used at lower volume for short campaigns focused on minimizing regret rather than obtaining a clean read. The candidate's wording applies the 'not a hard cutoff' qualification generally to both A/B/n and bandit work, which overextends the stated caveat.

The less-than-300-orders threshold and qualitative/big-swing recommendation appear only in the prefatory Topics overview, rather than in the substantive research document. That overview can establish that volume-based experimentation is a topic, but does not substantiate this operational playbook.

The exclusion broadens the source's wording. The overview reserves 'complex A/B/n testing, multi-armed bandits, and CUPED variance reduction' for 3,000+ orders/month; it does not categorically exclude all 'complex A/B tests' at low volume.
The source expressly defines the peeking pattern as continuously checking results and stopping once p < 0.05, and expressly states that it inflates the false-positive rate to over 26%.
The candidate does not generalize that numerical rate to other alpha levels or stopping rules.
SRM, flicker/FOOC, and Twyman's Law are named in the prefatory overview as issues relevant to statistically valid lifts rather than instrumentation artifacts.

The candidate converts that overview into a mandatory operational check without a substantive procedure or criterion in the supplied research text. It also treats Twyman's Law as equivalent to a specific experiment invalidation, whereas the excerpt's later definition describes it as a warning that surprising figures are usually wrong and may be caused by bugs or SRM.
The asserted Shopify platform behavior and named implementation alternatives occur only in the prefatory 'Look for' overview, not in a substantive section of the supplied research document.

That overview cannot certify the operational claim that client-side checkout testing is prevented or that Shopify Rollouts and Checkout Blocks are the required usable alternatives; the excerpt supplies no implementation conditions, scope, or limitations for either tool.

The substantive text states that fixed-horizon frequentist testing fixes the sample size in advance and looks once at the end, and that p-values and confidence levels are valid only under that assumption.
The candidate appropriately leaves non-fixed-horizon adjustments unspecified.
The substantive multi-variant/bandit discussion expressly states that bandits need volume to learn before they exploit.
The candidate does not invent a volume threshold that the source does not quantify.
The substantive pre-post discussion explicitly identifies the listed time confounders and states that the central risk is bias, not merely wider variance.
The candidate's limitation that the source gives no method to fully control every confounder is accurate.
The recommendation to replace ICE with PXL and the assertion that PXL calculates an experiment's 'true expected value' occur only in the prefatory Topics overview.

The supplied substantive text provides neither the PXL model nor an expected-value method. The overview may identify prioritization as a topic, but does not support this actionable implementation recommendation.

The prefatory overview expressly identifies personalized price testing as involving ethical/legal landmines. The candidate remains a high-level warning and does not claim specific legal requirements, jurisdictions, or mitigation steps.

omissions.description: The module-boundary guidance distinguishing CRO experimentation from page design and ordinary tracking work is not represented.
omissions.quote: CRO in this module means "is the difference real": statistics, experiment design, experimentation discipline. It is not page design (that is LPG) and not tracking accuracy (that is MEA), except where tracking breakage invalidates an experiment.

omissions.description: The specific definition and diagnostic implication of Twyman's Law is not represented; merely naming it as an invalidation does not capture this warning.
omissions.quote: The definition of Twyman's Law: any figure that looks incredibly interesting or surprising (e.g., a 364% lift) is usually wrong and likely caused by a tracking bug or Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM).

source_limitations: The excerpt ends immediately after the opening fixed-horizon paragraph, so it does not provide the continuation of the stopping-rules section or substantive procedures for sequential testing alternatives.

Several claims about Shopify checkout behavior, SRM/flicker/Twyman handling, low-volume playbooks, and PXL appear only in prefatory Topics or Look for summaries rather than in the substantive research section.

The document is labeled a synthesised research document and cites external sources, but the cited source materials are not included; their calculations, attributions, and any current platform behavior cannot be independently verified from this excerpt.
